# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

export const isOpaque = id => BLOCKS[id]?.opaque === true
export const isLiquid = id => id === B.LAVA || id === B.WATER || id === B.HONEY
export const isEmissive = id => Array.isArray(BLOCKS[id]?.emissive)

export function tileFor(id, face) {
  const b = BLOCKS[id]
  if (!b || b.tile < 0) return 0
  if (face === 3 && b.top != null) return b.top
  if (face === 2 && b.bottom != null) return b.bottom
  if (b.side != null && face !== 3 && face !== 2) return b.side
  return b.tile
}

- moon sprites.
- aurora: curved planes? Use a few large planes with additive rainbow texture at y=80 far away. Maybe simpler in sky shader with bands.

Sky shader:
```
varying vec3 vWorld;
vertex: vWorld = position;
frag:
 vec3 d = normalize(vWorld);
 float h = clamp(d.y*0.5+0.5,0,1);
 vec3 col = mix(horizon, zenith, pow(max(d.y,0),0.6));
 col = mix(bottom, col, smoothstep(-0.1,0.2,d.y));
 stars: hash on direction grid? use noise from d.xz*200, sparkle.
 aurora bands: sin(d.x*... + time) etc with rainbow tint near horizon.
 sun/moon glow near `uMoonDir`.
```
Can render moon in sky shader itself: compute dot(d, moonDir), draw circle with distorted smiley: use 2D vector from moon center approximated by tangent plane. Complex but possible:
```
float md = dot(d, uMoonDir);
if (md > 0.985) { vec2 uv = vec2(dot(d,right), dot(d,up))/0.015; ... }
```
Tangent basis computed from moonDir. Draw face inside circle with eyes/grin using smoothstep and distance. This would be high quality and no sprite. But sprite easier for detailed canvas.

Use sky shader + sprite moon. The sprite position at fixed world coordinate (e.g. -130, 175, -260) and scale 65; but camera moves only ~64; fine. At surface it's visible. In underground, blocked by world geometry. Sprite with fog false. Add glow sprite.

- Update moon orbit based on day time: moonGroup.position = center + direction*300. Simpler rotate around Y at high y. Since sky sphere static. Use group rotation y = time * 0.05; moon sprite at local (-180,180,-160) in group; camera sees. Could also fluctuate.
- We can set `skyMat.uniforms.uTime` and colors based on day time.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D action-survival sandbox inspired by Terraria’s getfixedboi/Zenith world, with hardcore combat, crafting, procedural terrain, and high-fidelity visuals.

## Requirements
- Start the player in the Underworld and provide an upward progression through hostile layers to the surface.
- Include fused biomes, destructible blocks, combat and bosses, crafting/inventory, survival systems, and responsive desktop/touch controls.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; verify the game with screenshots.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser game using Three.js and Vite, with procedural textures, voxel terrain, synthesized audio, custom UI, and a debug API.
- Used a compact procedurally generated world and a curated starting inventory to make the sandbox playable immediately.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game structure, UI, world generation, player controls, combat/entities, crafting/items, effects, and audio.
- Fixed several runtime issues, including UI element aliases and transparent voxel shader attributes.
- Verified `npm run build` successfully after the latest code edits.

### Active
- Refine and verify the in-game visuals and gameplay; recent changes adjusted lighting, reduced emissive intensity, expanded the starting island, and added lava falls.
- Capture/read a fresh screenshot and test core interactions after the latest world-generation changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and inspect the output for any errors after the latest edits.
2. Launch the game and capture a fresh JPEG screenshot; check the spawn area and island/lava presentation.
3. Exercise movement, mining, combat, crafting, and boss interactions; fix any issues found.
4. Summarize assumptions and controls when reporting completion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page and UI markup.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `src/main.js`: Game initialization, loop, and debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural voxel world, generation, and chunk rendering.
- `src/player.js`: Player movement, controls, combat, and avatar.
- `src/entities.js`: Enemies, projectiles, and bosses.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, and input bindings.
- `src/blocks.js`: Block definitions and material properties.
- `src/items.js`: Items, recipes, and hotbar.
- `src/fx.js`: Lighting, atmosphere, particles, and post-processing.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural texture atlas and maps.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambience.
- `src/style.css`: Game UI styling.
- `screenshots/`: Existing screenshots from visual checks; these predate the latest world edits.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.
- The latest shell command ran `npm run build >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo built` and reported `built`.
- `window.__ZENITH` exposes gameplay/debug helpers, including `teleport`, `summon`, `god`, and `stats`; it now also exposes `THREE`.
- The user supplied attachment URL `https://omgithub.com/api/issue-attachments/e25b0706-db4e-410c-92c2-29f9afe672ac`; fetching it failed.
- Existing screenshots were captured before the final island/lava adjustments, so visual verification is still needed.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D action-survival sandbox inspired by Terraria’s getfixedboi/Zenith world, with hardcore combat, crafting, procedural terrain, and high-fidelity visuals.

## Requirements
- Start in the Underworld and progress upward through hostile layers to the surface.
- Include fused biomes, destructible blocks, combat and bosses, crafting/inventory, survival systems, and responsive desktop/touch controls.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; verify the game with screenshots.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser game using Three.js and Vite, with procedural textures, voxel terrain, synthesized audio, custom UI, and a debug API.
- Created a curated starting inventory and a hand-authored Underworld cathedral spawn area to make the sandbox playable immediately.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game structure, UI, world generation, player controls, combat/entities, crafting/items, effects, and audio.
- Fixed runtime issues including UI element aliases and transparent voxel shader attributes.
- Added a starting cathedral with masonry, lava features, braziers, banners, a life crystal, and lighting adjustments.
- `npm run build` succeeded after the latest edits.

### Active
- Inspect the latest screenshot, `screenshots/pass8.png`, and refine the spawn area if needed.
- Verify movement, mining, combat, crafting, and boss interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect `screenshots/pass8.png` for the latest spawn presentation.
2. Run `npm run build` and check for errors.
3. Exercise core gameplay interactions and fix any issues.
4. Summarize controls and assumptions when reporting completion.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game initialization, loop, and debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural voxel world and hand-authored spawn cathedral.
- `src/player.js`: Player movement, combat, lighting, and viewmodel.
- `src/entities.js`: Enemies, projectiles, and bosses.
- `src/fx.js`: Lighting, atmosphere, particles, banners, and post-processing.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, and input bindings.
- `src/blocks.js`: Block definitions and material properties.
- `src/items.js`: Items, recipes, and hotbar.
- `src/style.css`: Game UI styling.
- `screenshots/`: Visual-check screenshots, including the latest `pass8.png`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.

- Latest browser check captured `screenshots/pass8.png`, but its visual content has not yet been inspected.

181:   setupInput() {
182:     const onKey = (e, down) => {
183:       if (e.code === 'Tab' || e.code === 'KeyH' || e.code === 'Escape') return
184:       this.keys[e.code] = down
185:       if (!down) return
186:       if (e.code.startsWith('Digit')) {
187:         const n = Number(e.code.slice(5)); if (n >= 1 && n <= 8) this.game.selectSlot(n - 1)
188:       }
189:       if (e.code === 'KeyF') this.tryPlace()
190:       if (e.code === 'KeyQ') this.dash()
191:       if (e.code === 'KeyG') this.grappleHook()
192:       if (e.code === 'KeyE') this.interact()
193:       if (e.code === 'KeyV') this.toggleView()
194:       if (e.code === 'KeyM') { this.game.audio.setMuted(!this.game.audio.muted); this.game.ui.toast(this.game.audio.muted ? 'Audio muted.' : 'Audio online.') }
195:       if (e.code === 'Space') this.jumpRequest = true
196:       if (e.code === 'KeyR') this.game.usePotion()
197:     }
198:     window.addEventListener('keydown', e => onKey(e, true))
199:     window.addEventListener('keyup', e => onKey(e, false))
200:     document.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {
201:       if (document.pointerLockElement === this.game.canvas) this.look(e.movementX, e.movementY)
202:     })
203:     this.game.canvas.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => e.preventDefault())
204:     document.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {
205:       if (this.game.paused || !this.alive) return
206:       if (e.button === 0) { this.mousePrimary = true; this.primary() }
207:       if (e.button === 2) { this.mouseSecondary = true; this.mineCd = 0 }
208:     })
209:     document.addEventListener('mouseup', e => {

212:         if (this.game.hotbar[this.game.selected] === 'Pickaxe') this.mouseSecondary = false

214:       if (e.button === 2) this.mouseSecondary = false

353:   /* ---------------- physics & update ---------------- */
354:   update(dt, time) {
355:     if (!this.alive) { this.updateCamera(dt); return }
356:     this.attackCd = Math.max(0, this.attackCd - dt); this.dashCd = Math.max(0, this.dashCd - dt)
357:     this.mineCd = Math.max(0, this.mineCd - dt); this.placeCd = Math.max(0, this.placeCd - dt); this.potionCd = Math.max(0, this.potionCd - dt)
358:     this.invuln = Math.max(0, this.invuln - dt); this.dashTimer = Math.max(0, this.dashTimer - dt)
359:     this.lastDamage += dt
360:     this.shake = Math.max(0, this.shake - dt * 2.2)
361:     this.viewKick = Math.max(0, this.viewKick - dt * 1.6)
362:     this.swing = Math.max(0, this.swing - dt * 4.2)
363:     this.gamepad()
364: 
365:     const forward = this.keys.KeyW ? 1 : 0, back = this.keys.KeyS ? 1 : 0
366:     const left = this.keys.KeyA ? 1 : 0, right = this.keys.KeyD ? 1 : 0
367:     let ix = right - left + this.touchMove.x
368:     let iz = forward - back + this.touchMove.y
369:     const mag = Math.hypot(ix, iz); if (mag > 1) { ix /= mag; iz /= mag }
370:     const sprint = this.keys.ShiftLeft || this.keys.ShiftRight
371:     const speed = (sprint ? 7.6 : 5.4) * (this.inLiquid ? .7 : 1)
372:     const fx = -Math.sin(this.yaw), fz = -Math.cos(this.yaw)
373:     const rx = Math.cos(this.yaw), rz = -Math.sin(this.yaw)
374:     const targetVx = (fx * iz + rx * ix) * speed
375:     const targetVz = (fz * iz + rz * ix) * speed
376:     const accel = this.grounded ? 16 : 6
377:     this.velocity.x = THREE.MathUtils.damp(this.velocity.x, targetVx, accel, dt)
378:     this.velocity.z = THREE.MathUtils.damp(this.velocity.z, targetVz, accel, dt)
379:     this.moveAmount = Math.min(1, Math.hypot(this.velocity.x, this.velocity.z) / 6)
380: 
381:     // flight / jump
382:     const space = this.keys.Space || this.touchMove.jump > 0 || this.jumpRequest
383:     if (this.jumpRequest && this.grounded) {
384:       this.velocity.y = 9.4; this.grounded = false; this.game.audio.jump()
385:       this.jumpRequest = false
386:     }
387:     if (space && !this.grounded && this.wings && this.flight > 0 && this.velocity.y < 8.5) {
388:       this.velocity.y += 34 * dt
389:       this.velocity.y = Math.min(this.velocity.y, this.wingsUpgraded ? 9.5 : 7.2)
390:       this.flight -= 21 * dt
391:       if (Math.sin(time * 24) > .7) this.game.fx.spawnBurst(this.position.clone().add(V(0, .3, 0)), 0xff8a40, 1, .5, .06)
392:     }
393:     if (this.grounded) this.flight = Math.min(this.maxFlight, this.flight + 34 * dt)
394:     this.jumpRequest = false
395: 
396:     this.velocity.y -= 25 * dt
397:     if (this.velocity.y < -34) this.velocity.y = -34
398:     if (this.keys.KeyC) this.velocity.y -= 18 * dt
399: 
400:     // grapple pull
401:     if (this.grapple) {
402:       this.grapple.time -= dt
403:       const to = this.grapple.point.clone().sub(this.camera.position)
404:       const dist = to.length()
405:       if (dist < 1.8 || this.grapple.time <= 0) this.releaseGrapple()
406:       else {
407:         const pull = to.normalize().multiplyScalar(38)
408:         this.velocity.addScaledVector(pull, dt)
409:         this.velocity.clampLength(0, 22)
410:         this.grapple.line.geometry.attributes.position.array[0] = this.camera.position.x
411:         this.grapple.line.geometry.attributes.position.array[1] = this.camera.position.y - .15
412:         this.grapple.line.geometry.attributes.position.array[2] = this.camera.position.z
413:         this.grapple.line.geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true
414:       }
415:     }
416: 
417:     const vBefore = this.velocity.y
418:     this.moveAndCollide(dt)
419:     if (this.grounded && vBefore < -17) {
420:       const dmg = Math.round((-vBefore - 17) * 5)
421:       if (dmg > 2) this.takeDamage(dmg, 'a lethal fall', this.position)
422:     }
423: 
424:     // liquids
425:     const atFeet = this.world.getBlock(this.position.x, this.position.y + .15, this.position.z)
426:     const atBody = this.world.getBlock(this.position.x, this.position.y + 1.1, this.position.z)
427:     this.inLiquid = atBody === B.WATER || atBody === B.HONEY || atFeet === B.WATER || atFeet === B.HONEY
428:     const inLava = atFeet === B.LAVA || atBody === B.LAVA || this.world.getBlock(this.position.x, this.position.y - .1, this.position.z) === B.LAVA
429:     if (inLava) {
430:       this.lavaTimer -= dt
431:       if (this.lavaTimer <= 0) {
432:         this.takeDamage(13, 'the molten Underworld', this.position, true)
433:         this.lavaTimer = .32

export const isSolid = id => BLOCKS[id]?.solid === true
export const isOpaque = id => BLOCKS[id]?.opaque === true
export const isLiquid = id => id === B.LAVA || id === B.WATER || id === B.HONEY
export const isEmissive = id => Array.isArray(BLOCKS[id]?.emissive)

export function tileFor(id, face) {
  const b = BLOCKS[id]
  if (!b || b.tile < 0) return 0
  if (face === 3 && b.top != null) return b.top
  if (face === 2 && b.bottom != null) return b.bottom
  if (b.side != null && face !== 3 && face !== 2) return b.side
  return b.tile
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Three.js browser game as a playable 3D action-survival sandbox inspired by Terraria’s Zenith/getfixedboi world.
- Verify its visuals and core gameplay, then report controls and reasonable assumptions.

## Requirements
- Start in the Underworld and progress upward through fused hostile biomes; support destructible blocks, combat, bosses, crafting, inventory, and survival systems.
- Provide dynamic atmospheric visuals and responsive desktop/touch controls.
- Verify gameplay and capture screenshots; the user’s latest request specifies small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use the existing Three.js/Vite project, procedural voxel world, synthesized audio, custom UI, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- Keep the curated starting inventory and hand-authored Underworld cathedral spawn for immediate playability.
- Reduce scene light counts and add staged quality reduction to improve performance.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game’s world generation, controls, combat/entities, crafting/items, UI, effects, and audio.
- Added the Underworld cathedral spawn, then fixed UI overlay animations, adjusted the first-person sword/viewmodel, corrected touch actions, and reduced visual light intensities.
- `npm run build` succeeded after the latest code edits.
- Browser checks confirmed the inventory opens visibly and the Eye of Cthulhu boss can be summoned; mining reached partial progress against an obsidian-brick block.

### Active
- Finish visual and functional verification, including combat, mining completion, and crafting/boss interactions.
- Investigate reported browser console 404s and the anomalous FPS/render statistics from automated checks.
- Review or recapture the latest visual checks as small JPEGs at the requested viewport size.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest visual state and recapture a small JPEG if needed.
2. Run gameplay checks for mining completion, combat damage, crafting, and boss interaction; fix issues uncovered.
3. Investigate console 404s and verify performance stats, then rebuild and summarize controls and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game setup, loop, quality scaling, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and hand-authored cathedral spawn.
- `src/player.js`: Movement, combat, lighting, and viewmodel.
- `src/entities.js`: Enemies, projectiles, and bosses.
- `src/fx.js`: Lighting, atmosphere, particles, and post-processing.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, and input bindings.
- `src/style.css`: Game UI styling and overlay behavior.
- `src/blocks.js`: Block definitions and material properties.
- `src/items.js`: Items, recipes, and hotbar.
- `screenshots/`: Existing visual-check screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.
- `window.__ZENITH` exposes gameplay/debug helpers such as `teleport`, `summon`, `god`, `stats`, `quality`, and `THREE`.
- Latest build succeeded, with a Vite warning that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Automated checks logged two `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)` errors; source not yet identified.
- Latest automated stats showed FPS as `1` and render calls/triangles as `1`; these values need validation.

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Three.js browser game as a playable 3D action-survival sandbox inspired by Terraria’s Zenith/getfixedboi world.
- Verify visuals and core gameplay, then report controls and reasonable assumptions.

## Requirements
- Start in the Underworld and progress upward through fused hostile biomes; support destructible blocks, combat, bosses, crafting, inventory, and survival systems.
- Provide dynamic atmospheric visuals and responsive desktop/touch controls.
- Verify gameplay and capture small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use the existing Three.js/Vite project, procedural voxel world, synthesized audio, custom UI, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- Keep the curated starting inventory and hand-authored Underworld cathedral spawn for immediate playability.
- Reduce scene light counts and add staged quality reduction to improve performance.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game’s world generation, controls, combat/entities, crafting/items, UI, effects, and audio.
- Added the Underworld cathedral spawn; fixed UI overlay animations, first-person sword/viewmodel, and touch actions; reduced visual light intensities.
- `npm run build` succeeded after the latest code edits.
- Browser checks confirmed inventory visibility and Eye of Cthulhu summoning; mining made partial progress against an obsidian-brick block.

### Active
- Finish visual and functional verification, including mining completion, combat, crafting, and boss interactions.
- Investigate browser console 404s and anomalous FPS/render statistics.
- Review or recapture the latest visual checks as small JPEGs at the requested viewport size.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest visual state and recapture a small JPEG if needed.
2. Run gameplay checks for mining completion, combat damage, crafting, and boss interaction; fix issues uncovered.
3. Investigate console 404s and validate performance stats, then rebuild and summarize controls and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game setup, loop, quality scaling, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world and hand-authored cathedral spawn.
- `src/player.js`: Movement, combat, lighting, and viewmodel.
- `src/entities.js`: Enemies, projectiles, and bosses.
- `src/fx.js`: Lighting, atmosphere, particles, and post-processing.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, and input bindings.
- `src/style.css`: Game UI styling and overlay behavior.
- `src/blocks.js`: Block definitions and material properties.
- `src/items.js`: Items, recipes, and hotbar.
- `screenshots/`: Existing visual-check screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.
- `window.__ZENITH` exposes helpers such as `teleport`, `summon`, `god`, `stats`, `quality`, and `THREE`.
- Latest build succeeded with a Vite warning that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Automated checks logged two `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)` errors; source is unidentified.
- Latest automated stats reported FPS `1` and render calls/triangles `1`; these values need validation.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Three.js browser game as a playable 3D action-survival sandbox inspired by Terraria’s Zenith/getfixedboi world.
- Verify visuals and core gameplay, then report controls and reasonable assumptions.

## Requirements
- Start in the Underworld and progress upward through fused hostile biomes; support destructible blocks, combat, bosses, crafting, inventory, and survival systems.
- Provide dynamic atmospheric visuals and responsive desktop/touch controls.
- Verify gameplay and capture small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use the existing Three.js/Vite project, procedural voxel world, synthesized audio, custom UI, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- Keep the curated starting inventory and hand-authored Underworld cathedral spawn for immediate playability.
- Reduce scene light counts and add staged quality reduction to improve performance.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game’s world generation, controls, combat/entities, crafting/items, UI, effects, and audio.
- Added the Underworld cathedral spawn; fixed UI overlay animations, first-person sword/viewmodel, and touch actions; reduced visual light intensities.
- `npm run build` succeeded before the latest browser checks; Vite warned the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- Captured `screenshots/final-check.jpg` at 1280×720.
- Confirmed inventory opening and Eye of Cthulhu summoning in prior checks.

### Active
- Complete functional verification for mining, combat damage, crafting, and boss interaction; latest test results were inconclusive because the simulation appeared paused (FPS `0`, render calls/triangles `1`).
- Investigate the remaining console error: `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`.
- Validate FPS/render statistics and inspect the captured screenshot; then rebuild and summarize controls and assumptions.

### Blocked
- Gameplay checks require a reliable way to keep the game simulation active in browser automation; mining did not complete and test interactions did not validate the gameplay loop.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/final-check.jpg` and confirm how browser focus/pointer lock affects `game.paused`.
2. Rerun mining, combat, crafting, and boss checks with gameplay unpaused; distinguish actual game defects from test setup issues.
3. Identify the 404 resource and verify render/FPS stats, then rebuild and report controls and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game setup, loop, quality scaling, pause handling, and `window.__ZENITH` debug API.
- `src/player.js`: Movement, combat, mining, and interaction behavior.
- `src/entities.js`: Enemies, projectiles, and bosses.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, and input bindings.
- `src/fx.js`: Lighting, atmosphere, particles, and post-processing.
- `screenshots/final-check.jpg`: Latest browser capture.
- `screenshots/`: Earlier visual-check screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was performed.
- Latest browser check reported FPS `0`, calls `1`, and triangles `1`; game pause/focus state may explain these readings.
- Mining targeted an obsidian-brick block but reached only `0.11` progress; no block was broken in that check.
- Boss summoning succeeded, but the test queried `boss.health` while the HUD reads `boss.hp` and `boss.maxHp`; damage was not verified.
- A god-mode test left health unchanged, so player damage handling was not independently verified.
